name: Maximum-Class Local Agreement Equivalence
hypotheses: A finite binary class presented by one selected forbidden pattern on every support of size $r+1$, with $1\le r<N$.
statement: The selected-pattern avoider attains the rank-$r$ Sauer bound exactly when all local agreement graphs on $(r+2)$-supports are connected.
proof: Connected agreement graphs make the signed ideal a polarization of the squarefree Veronese ideal. Its multigraded Hilbert series then counts exactly $\sum_{j=0}^r\binom Nj$ full words, and the selected forbidden patterns prevent VC dimension above $r$. Conversely, project a maximum avoider to any $(r+2)$-support. The complementary class has $r+3$ words and contains one edge in each direction supplied by the selected patterns. Those edges form an acyclic graph, so cardinality forces them to be connected; their edge-intersection graph is the local agreement graph.
